content.figure_caption: Figure 5: The A.C.S. assessment for the initial evaluation of patients with suspected acute coronary syndrome. ECG, electrocardiogram.
content.figure_summary: A.C.S. stands for Abnormal ECG? Clinical Context? Stable Patient? Abnormal ECG: perform an ECG within 10 minutes of FMC and assess for evidence of ischaemia or other abnormalities. Clinical Context: consider the patient's presentation, history and available investigations. Stable Patient: rapidly assess clinical and vital stability including heart rate, blood pressure and oxygen saturations and check for signs of cardiogenic shock (CS).
content.recommendations: Perform an ECG immediately on first medical contact (FMC) and interpret within 10 minutes. Repeat ECG as necessary, particularly if symptoms have waned at FMC.
content.section_3_2_summary: The resting 12-lead ECG is the first-line diagnostic tool for suspected ACS. It is recommended that an ECG is obtained immediately upon FMC and interpreted by a qualified emergency medical technician or physician within 10 minutes. Based on the initial ECG, patients with suspected ACS can be differentiated into working diagnoses (details follow in the guideline).
